## R326-001 — A timed-out final fragment is silently lost at EOF

`crates/cli/src/daemon_log.rs:178-196`, `pump`, the `Ok(0) => finish()` arm: `read_until` appends consumed bytes to `line` even when it subsequently returns a timeout. The timeout branch correctly retains those bytes. If the writer then shuts down without adding bytes, the next call returns `Ok(0)` (zero newly read bytes), and this arm finishes without passing the retained fragment to `Shared::line`.

Normal-use witness: write `ready\n\xffsplit`, leave the stream idle for three read-recheck intervals, then `shutdown(Write)`. At this head the sink contains only `ready\n`; `\xffsplit` disappears. Completing the fragment with ` continuation\nlast\n` after the same idle interval preserves it once. All 22 shipped daemon-log tests pass, so their immediate split-write/shutdown cases do not defend this edge.

Required repair: at EOF, send a nonempty retained `line` through the ordinary shared sink before finishing. Add timeout-to-EOF and timeout-to-continuation regressions, including byte-exact/non-UTF-8 output. Do not emit the fragment on every timeout; that would split a still-live logical line.

## Answers to the packet

- **Diagnosis:** credible empirical justification for bounding socket reads. I inspected the hung-child sample, stress driver, standalone probe and retained counts: author's before 4/20,000 hangs, after 0/20,000 and 0/5,000; 25 shared-build runs pass. This is not an independently reproduced kernel defect or proof of its exact incidence. One wording correction: stdout's field drop shuts its writer down and joins first; stderr's field drop has not yet happened, so the sampled stderr reader waiting in `recv` is expected, not a second demonstrated missed shutdown. The standalone probe's `fragment || !line.is_empty()` counts retained memory as success; it does not prove sink delivery and misses R326-001.
- **Other log tests:** inspected all 22. The payload and repetition tests put the writer on a separate thread while the caller pumps; the window test puts the reader on another thread; inherited-writer teardown uses the real reader thread; process-wide panic capture is re-executed in its own child. No writer/reader same-thread deadlock was found. The new panic parent has a scaled 60-second child budget and kills only its own child PID.
- **Watchdog scope/lifecycle:** job control creates distinct cargo and watchdog process groups. Exact-head probes verified cargo PGID equals the launched PID, timeout exit 8, no later `--then`, no surviving recorded cargo/test/sleep PIDs, lock release, and a same-named bystander outside the group surviving. SIGINT/TERM/HUP with an armed watchdog returned 130/143/129 and released only after cleanup. Quick multi-command, slow non-test, limit 0, six malformed limit/scale cases and eight deadline-adjacent runs passed. The current code handles USR2-interrupted waits and retries cargo status when the group has already ended. No claim that SIGKILL can release a lock.
- **Composition/configuration:** niceness 19, incremental off and 4/4 job/thread caps reached the fake cargo; floor, stamp and lock ownership logic remains before/around the same batch. Default 20 minutes, scale, `Ns`, `0` and exit 8 are documented in AGENTS.md and the script header. Negative/nonintegral limits and scale below 1 refuse before lock/cargo.
- **Policy/brake:** elapsed-time termination is a POLICY on the owned run's duration, not a one-directional do-not-kill BRAKE: removing it kills less. READ_RECHECK is a liveness/recheck bound, not a destructive retention rule; the packet's brake label is not needed to justify it.
- **Cost:** new daemon work is up to two idle socket timeout wakeups/second per daemon, not per seat, no daemon process launch. One watchdog group plus its sleep is started per bounded cargo-test command; timeout takes one process-table snapshot. `stop_watchdog` also polls group disappearance using 50-ms sleeps during cleanup, so the launch row should mention that bounded-lifecycle polling rather than imply exactly one sleep launch per command. No new fleet-wide loop.
